newsitem.title: USA: Farrakhan says he'll sit out presidential election.
newsitem.headline: Farrakhan says he'll sit out presidential election.

text.p: Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, in an interview published on Tuesday, said he is sitting out the presidential election and will not urge his followers to vote for any candidate.

"I would tell our people to vote their conscience ... I would not discourage our people from voting but I don't see any candidate that is worthy of my vote," he told the Chicago Sun-Times. "I really don't see anyone that is in the best interest of our people and an agenda that is in the best interest of the masses."
Farrakhan organised the Million Man March that drew hundreds of thousands of black men to Washington a year ago and was viewed at the time as a potential force in swaying a portion of the black vote.
Since the march, he has made controversial visits to Libya, Cuba, Iraq, Iran, Nigeria and Sudan, some of which Washington has branded as supporting terrorism.

The U.S. Treasury Department barred him from accepting a $250,000 human rights award in Libya or $1 billion that Muammar Gaddafi, the Libyan leader, had pledged to the Nation of Islam after meeting Farrakhan in January.
The Nation of Islam is thought to have about 10,000 active members.
